You are a research + architecture agent. Nicholas runs Nxeon, a Next.js (App Router) + Prisma + Postgres platform at /opt/nxeon. He is building several new products, each as (a) its own standalone app AND (b) an add-on module inside the Nxeon admin portal — Nxeon is his central hub. Assume new apps use Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Prisma + Postgres, deployable on his dev box 51.79.226.215.

YOUR PROJECT: "Ads Autopilot" — a SaaS that manages and automates a company's paid advertising across Meta (Facebook/Instagram), TikTok, and Google Ads. Connect a client's ad accounts, then run/optimize campaigns: budget pacing, rules automation, creative rotation/testing, AI creative generation, and unified cross-platform reporting.

THIS ROUND IS RESEARCH + PLANNING ONLY. Hard guardrails — DO NOT: write application code, modify /opt/nxeon, write to any database, call any external API, send anything, or deploy. Research and plan only.

Use WebSearch/WebFetch heavily. Research at least, ACCURATELY (this is the crux): (1) Meta Marketing API — access tiers, app review, business verification, standard vs advanced access, capabilities, rate limits; (2) TikTok Marketing/Business API — developer app approval, capabilities, limits; (3) Google Ads API — developer token levels (test vs basic vs standard), MCC/manager account, OAuth, approval process + timeline; for all three note the APPROVAL LEAD TIME and prerequisites (this is a long-pole item — flag it prominently). (4) Capabilities each API gives for campaign/adset/ad CRUD, creative upload, budgets, insights/reporting. (5) Competitors: Madgicx, Revealbot, AdEspresso, Smartly.io, Metadata — what they do, pricing. (6) Automation/rules engine design and budget-pacing logic. (7) Compliance: each platform's automation/policy rules, data handling/PII. Note that ad creative generation can reuse existing Nxeon ad-creative tooling.

Deliverables (write to disk, then return a ≤200-word summary):
1. /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/ads/architecture.md — thorough: product overview, competitors & positioning, the exact API access requirements + approval timelines per platform (links + pricing), recommended tech stack, unified data model (accounts/campaigns/adsets/ads/creatives/insights), automation/rules engine design, reporting, how it runs standalone AND as a Nxeon admin add-on, phased build plan, key risks, compliance. Cite sources.
2. /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/ads/board.json — JSON board spec: {"board":{"name":"Ads Autopilot","color":"#22D3EE"},"columns":[{"name":"Research","cards":[{"title":"...","label":"...","body":"markdown detailed"}]}, ...]} columns exactly: Research, Ideas, Backlog, Phase 1, Later, Done. 18-35 cards, each actionable. Valid JSON only.

Return only your ≤200-word summary (paths + headline findings + the biggest blocker, especially API-approval timelines).

## Developer Token Access Levels and Timeline

After signing up, your token is pending approval. You can use your developer token immediately with a test manager account. However, your developer token must be approved before you can use it with production Google Ads accounts.

### Manager Account Requirements

Developer tokens are tied to a Google Ads manager account (MCC) and must be approved by Google before API access is granted.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of Meta Marketing API standard access vs advanced access, app review, and business verification in 2026:

## Standard Access vs Advanced Access

Every new app starts on Standard Access, which is effectively the free, entry-level tier. Standard Access limits you to basic permissions and testing against your own accounts. Standard access is available immediately after creating a Meta app and adding the Marketing API product, and allows API calls to ad accounts you own or have admin access to, with rate limits based on spend tier.

You can't launch at scale for real users until you clear a second review round for Advanced Access. Advanced access enables broader permissions — such as managing ads on behalf of third-party advertisers — and requires formal App Review with Meta's compliance team.

## Business Verification

Business Verification is mandatory if you need Advanced Access to ads_management or if you want to create ad accounts programmatically. The process usually takes a few business days.

## App Review Requirements

Advanced Access (Full Access on the Marketing API) requires App Review, business verification, and a screencast that demonstrates each permission in your live product.

The app owner's Meta Business Manager must be verified with legal business documents before any Advanced Access submission can proceed. Additionally, for ads_management Advanced Access, Meta expects a working client account onboarding flow — the mechanism by which another business grants the app access to their ad data, as an app that only touches the developer's own test accounts does not demonstrate the client-facing use case the permission exists for.

## Note on 2026 Changes

It's worth noting that on May 4, 2026, Meta renamed "Ads Management Standard Access" (AMSA) to the Marketing API Access Tier and restructured it into two levels: Limited Access and Full Access.

Here are the search results for TikTok Marketing API business developer app approval process, capabilities, and rate limits:

## App Approval Process

Access requires developer registration, app creation, a review process, and approval — which can take 3–7 days. However, basic Marketing API access can be approved within a few business days for established business accounts with ad history. More advanced access tiers — like content posting or higher rate limit tiers — can take one to three weeks, especially if TikTok requests additional documentation about your use case or data practices.

TikTok requires Business Center onboarding, sandbox-to-production app review, business verification for higher-volume access, and a data-security compliance audit.

## Capabilities

The TikTok Marketing API supports campaign management, reporting, and audience operations. The Content Posting API requires proper scopes, user consent, and (for broader visibility) passing TikTok's audit process. Unaudited apps may have their published content restricted to private visibility. Build compliance gates into your automation workflows — don't skip the audit step if you're publishing at scale.

## Rate Limits

Request rate calculation is based on a one minute sliding window. With 600 RPM per-endpoint baselines and per-app, per-token, and per-advertiser quotas in play, multi-tenant SaaS needs centralized request pacing rather than per-tenant throttling alone.

For specific APIs: The Content Posting API enforces a limit of 6 requests per minute per user access token and 25 videos per account per day. The Research API daily limit of 1,000 requests per day is currently fixed.

TikTok reviews quota-increase requests for the Display API and Content Posting API on a case-by-case basis. There is no self-serve upgrade path and no published SLA for approval timelines.

# Ads Autopilot — Architecture & Product Plan

_Research + planning document. Prepared 2026-08-10. No code, no external API calls, no deployment — planning only._

---

## 1. Product Overview

**Ads Autopilot** is a SaaS that connects a company's paid-ad accounts across **Meta (Facebook/Instagram), TikTok, and Google Ads**, then runs and optimizes campaigns from one control plane:

- **Account connection** — OAuth into each platform, discover ad accounts, campaigns, ad sets/groups, ads.
- **Budget pacing** — keep spend on a target curve; prevent the classic 2x/day and 30.4x/month overspends.
- **Rules automation** — "if CPA > X for 3 days, pause"; scheduled dayparting; auto-scaling of winners.
- **Creative rotation / A-B testing** — rotate, promote winners, retire fatigued creatives.
- **AI creative generation** — reuse Nxeon's existing ad-creative tooling to generate images/copy variants.
- **Unified cross-platform reporting** — one schema, one dashboard, apples-to-apples across the three networks.

It ships **two ways**: (a) a standalone Next.js app on the dev box (`51.79.226.215`), and (b) an add-on module inside the Nxeon admin portal (Nxeon is the central hub).

---

## 2. Competitors & Positioning

| Tool | Focus | Pricing (2026) |
|---|---|---|
| **Madgicx** | Meta-only AI optimization + creative/audience insight | from ~$49/mo, ad-spend tiered |
| **Revealbot** | Granular rule-based automation across Meta, Google, TikTok | from ~$99/mo, ad-spend tiered |
| **AdEspresso** | SMB-friendly split-testing UX over Meta + Google | from ~$49/mo, per-account |
| **Smartly.io** | Enterprise cross-channel creative + campaign orchestration | unpublished; ~$5k/mo floor, ~$90k median annual |
| **Metadata.io** | B2B, revenue/pipeline-optimized, multi-channel (LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Bing, Reddit), AI agents | custom; reports of ~$60k |

**Positioning gap Ads Autopilot targets:** Revealbot has the automation but is a bare rules engine; Madgicx is Meta-only; Smartly/Metadata are enterprise-priced. **Ads Autopilot = Revealbot-class cross-platform automation + built-in AI creative generation (via Nxeon), at SMB/agency pricing, bundled into the Nxeon hosting/marketing ecosystem** as a differentiator (existing Nxeon customers get ads managed where their site already lives).

Sources: [Smartly vs Madgicx](https://admanage.ai/blog/smartly-vs-madgicx), [Meta ads automation pricing](https://adlibrary.com/guides/meta-ads-automation-software-pricing-9-options-compared), [Madgicx review](https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/madgicx-review-2026-meta-ads-alternatives), [Metadata.io review](https://saleshive.com/vendors/metadata-io).

---

## 3. API Access Requirements & Approval Timelines — **THE LONG POLE**

> **BIGGEST BLOCKER: API approvals gate the entire product.** Nothing beyond a self-account demo works until these clear. Meta advanced access + business verification and Google Ads Basic/Standard access are the critical path — **budget 4–8 weeks of calendar time, start Day 1, in parallel.** All three require a legal business entity, a verified business, a public privacy policy + working product demo/screencast, and a real client-onboarding flow (not just your own accounts).

### 3.1 Meta Marketing API
- **Tiers:** Every new app starts on **Standard Access** (dev tier) — only your own/admin ad accounts, ~60-point rate quota. **Advanced Access** (standard tier) is required to manage *third-party* clients' ads and unlocks the ~9,000-point quota. (Note: on 2026-05-04 Meta renamed AMSA to "Marketing API Access Tier" with **Limited vs Full Access** levels.)
- **Requirements for Advanced/Full:** formal **App Review**, **Business Verification** (legal docs; mandatory for `ads_management` advanced access and for programmatic ad-account creation), a **screencast demonstrating each permission live**, a **working client-onboarding flow**, and a public privacy policy.
- **Permissions:** `ads_management`, `ads_read`, `business_management`, `pages_read_engagement`/`pages_manage_ads` as needed.
- **Timeline:** Business Verification a few business days; App Review commonly **1–3+ weeks**, longer if the reviewer bounces the screencast. Plan for iteration.
- **Rate limits:** Business-Use-Case (BUC) point system, separate pools for `ads_insights` vs `ads_management`; hard cap 100 POST/sec; heavy insight pulls with breakdowns cost more points. Design centralized pacing.

Sources: [Meta app review guide](https://singhamandeep.com/facebook-ads-api-permission-app-review/), [Advanced access](https://singhamandeep.com/what-is-meta-advanced-access/), [Access levels for agencies](https://www.adamigo.ai/blog/meta-ads-api-access-levels-for-agencies), [Meta rate limiting docs](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/overview/rate-limiting/), [AdManage limits](https://admanage.ai/blog/meta-ads-api).

### 3.2 Google Ads API
- **Developer token levels (per official docs):**
  - **Test Account** — test accounts only, 15,000 ops/day. Immediate.
  - **Explorer** — test + production, **2,880 ops/day** on production. Often auto-granted.
  - **Basic** — test + production, 15,000 ops/day. **~5 business-day review.**
  - **Standard** — unlimited for most services. **~10 business-day review**; for large/multi-user tools; needs demo + Required Minimum Functionality compliance.
- **Prerequisites:** token is tied to a **Manager (MCC) account**; **OAuth 2.0** per client; Google Cloud project. A **brand-verification pilot (launched 2026-07-07)** can cut a pending review from days to hours.
- **Timeline:** token approval typically **5–14 business days**; brand verification may shortcut. Start with test account immediately.

Sources: [Access levels](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/access-levels), [Developer token](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/get-started/dev-token), [Basic access guide](https://www.slobodan-jelisavac.com/en/blog/google-ads-api-basic-access-guide).

### 3.3 TikTok Marketing API
- **Access:** developer registration → app creation → **Business Center onboarding** → sandbox-to-production **app review** → business verification for higher volume → data-security compliance audit.
- **Capabilities:** campaign management, reporting, audience operations; v1.3 with OAuth. (Content Posting API is separate, needs audit; not core to ads mgmt.)
- **Timeline:** basic Marketing API **~3–7 business days** (faster for established business accounts with ad history); advanced/high-volume tiers **1–3 weeks**; quota increases are case-by-case with **no self-serve path and no published SLA**.
- **Rate limits:** 1-minute sliding window, ~600 RPM/endpoint baseline; per-app, per-token, per-advertiser quotas → needs **centralized request pacing**.

Sources: [TikTok rate limits](https://www.getphyllo.com/post/tiktok-api-rate-limits-in-2026-quotas-errors-workarounds), [Marketing API v1.3](https://soku.ai/blog/tiktok-marketing-api-v1-3-explained), [Business API setup](https://tiktok.savvyshopperhubs.com/tiktok-business-api-guide/).

### 3.4 API Capability Matrix (all three broadly support)
| Capability | Meta | Google Ads | TikTok |
|---|---|---|---|
| Campaign/AdSet(Group)/Ad CRUD | ✅ | ✅ (mutate ops) | ✅ |
| Budget get/set | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Creative upload (image/video) | ✅ | ✅ (assets) | ✅ |
| Insights/reporting | ✅ (BUC insights) | ✅ (GAQL) | ✅ |
| Audiences | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Recommendations | limited | ✅ (recommendations) | limited |

Sources: [Google GAQL](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/query/overview), [Google mutate best practices](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/mutating/best-practices), [Opteo google-ads-api lib](https://github.com/Opteo/google-ads-api).

---

## 4. Recommended Tech Stack

- **App:** Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript (matches Nxeon).
- **DB/ORM:** Postgres + Prisma.
- **Background jobs:** durable queue for pacing/rules ticks and insight syncs — BullMQ + Redis, or pg-boss (Postgres-native, one less dependency). Cron-style scheduler for periodic evaluation.
- **API clients:** official/community SDKs — `google-ads-api` (Opteo) for Google; typed fetch wrappers for Meta Graph and TikTok v1.3 (versioned).
- **Auth:** platform OAuth per client account; encrypted token vault (KMS or libsodium-sealed columns); auto-refresh worker.
- **Rate limiting:** centralized token-bucket per platform + per ad account, respecting BUC points (Meta), ops/day (Google), RPM windows (TikTok).
- **AI creative:** reuse **existing Nxeon ad-creative tooling** — do not rebuild.
- **Frontend:** React server components + a charting lib for reporting; shadcn/Tailwind to match Nxeon theme (brand cyan `#22D3EE`).
- **Observability:** structured logs + per-account API-quota dashboards; audit log of every mutation (compliance requirement).

---

## 5. Unified Data Model

Normalize all three platforms into one schema (platform-specific fields in a `raw JSONB` column).

```
Organization ─┐
              ├─< AdAccountConnection (platform enum, oauth tokens enc, external_account_id, status)
              │        └─< Campaign (external_id, objective, status, budget, budget_type)
              │              └─< AdSet   (a.k.a. AdGroup; targeting JSONB, budget, schedule)
              │                    └─< Ad (external_id, status, creative_id)
              ├─< Creative (type: image|video|carousel, asset_url, source: uploaded|ai_generated, nxeon_asset_ref)
              ├─< InsightSnapshot (entity_type, entity_id, date, impressions, clicks, spend, conversions, revenue, cpa, roas, ctr, cpm)  ← time-series
              ├─< Rule (name, scope, condition JSON, action JSON, schedule, enabled, last_run)
              ├─< RuleExecution (rule_id, entity_id, evaluated_at, matched, action_taken, result)
              ├─< BudgetPlan (entity_id, period, target_spend, pacing_strategy, cap)
              └─< AuditLog (actor, action, entity, before/after JSONB, platform_response)
```

Key notes: `platform` enum {META, GOOGLE, TIKTOK}; keep a canonical metric set + `raw` JSONB for platform extras; store currency + timezone per account (pacing math depends on account TZ); `InsightSnapshot` is the reporting fact table (daily grain, backfilled + incrementally synced).

---

## 6. Automation / Rules Engine Design

**Model:** each Rule = `{ scope (account/campaign/adset/ad, with filters), condition tree (AND/OR of metric comparisons over a lookback window), action, schedule, guardrails }`.

- **Conditions:** metric (spend, CPA, ROAS, CTR, freq, conv) `op` threshold, over lookback (today / 3d / 7d), optional min-impressions floor to avoid acting on noise.
- **Actions:** pause/enable, adjust budget ±%/abs, adjust bid, rotate/pause creative, send alert (Nxeon notification/email), tag.
- **Scheduler:** evaluation ticks (e.g., every 15–60 min) pull latest insights → evaluate rules → enqueue mutations → write RuleExecution + AuditLog. Idempotent; dry-run mode.
- **Safety guardrails:** max budget-change per day, cooldown between actions on same entity, global kill-switch, require insights freshness before acting, never act below a statistical-significance floor.
- **Example:** "If campaign pacing ≥10% behind target on/after day 20 and ROAS ≥ target → raise daily budget +20%." (mirrors industry pattern).

**Budget pacing logic:**
- Target curve = `target_period_spend × (elapsed_time_in_period / total_time)`, adjusted for dayparting weights.
- Each tick compute `pace_ratio = actual_spend / expected_spend`; if ahead → throttle daily budget / shift to standard delivery; if behind (and performance healthy) → raise budget toward cap.
- **Overspend guards:** respect platform realities — Google can spend up to **2x daily / 30.4x monthly**; enforce hard monthly cap by auto-pausing when projected month-end > cap. Daypart toward converting hours.

Sources: [Google budget pacing formula](https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/google-ads-daily-and-monthly-budget-pacing-rules), [FB budget pacing](https://wevion.ai/en/blog/budget-pacing-facebook-ads-guide/), [overspend prevention](https://ustechautomations.com/resources/blog/reduce-automated-campaign-budget-alerts-overspend-prevention-with-automation-2026).

---

## 7. Reporting

- **Fact table:** `InsightSnapshot` (daily grain) synced incrementally; hourly for pacing-critical accounts.
- **Unified metrics:** spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, CPM, CPC, conversions, CPA, revenue, ROAS — normalized across platforms with a documented mapping (attribution windows differ per platform → label them).
- **Views:** cross-platform overview, per-platform drilldown, creative leaderboard, pacing/burn-down vs target, rule-activity feed, client-facing exportable reports (PDF/CSV).
- Cache aggregates; never hit live APIs on dashboard load (rate limits).

---

## 8. Standalone AND Nxeon Add-on

**Shared core:** put all platform clients, data model, rules engine, pacing, and sync workers in a **framework-agnostic core package** (`@ads-autopilot/core`) that neither UI depends on directly.

- **Standalone app:** own Next.js app + own Postgres on the dev box; own auth/billing; full multi-tenant SaaS.
- **Nxeon add-on:** mount as a module under `/admin/ads` in the Nxeon portal; reuse Nxeon auth, org model, notifications, billing, **and the AI ad-creative tooling**; the core package is imported and its workers run on Nxeon's job infra. Feature-flag it (`ENABLE_ADS_AUTOPILOT`) like other Nxeon modules until API access + security review pass.
- **Data:** either a shared schema namespaced (`ads_*` tables) inside Nxeon's DB, or a separate DB with the same Prisma schema — keep the migration reversible. Match Nxeon theme (cyan `#22D3EE`).

---

## 9. Phased Build Plan

- **Phase 0 — Approvals & legal (Day 1, parallel, long-pole):** register apps, submit Meta business verification + app review, apply Google dev token (start on test), TikTok Business Center + app review. Draft privacy policy, ToS, data-handling doc. Build the demo/screencast flow reviewers require.
- **Phase 1 — Foundation + Meta read-only:** core package, data model, OAuth + token vault, Meta account/campaign/insight **sync (read)**, unified reporting dashboard, Nxeon `/admin/ads` shell. (Works under Standard access on own accounts.)
- **Phase 2 — Google + TikTok connectors:** add both platforms behind the same schema; unified cross-platform reporting.
- **Phase 3 — Write ops + rules engine:** mutations (pause/budget/bid), rules engine + scheduler, guardrails, audit log, dry-run.
- **Phase 4 — Budget pacing + creative:** pacing engine, dayparting, overspend guards; creative rotation/testing; AI creative generation via Nxeon tooling.
- **Phase 5 — Multi-tenant polish:** client onboarding flow, billing, alerts, exportable client reports, per-account quota dashboards.

---

## 10. Key Risks

1. **API approvals slip the whole timeline** (see §3) — mitigate: start Day 1, keep read-only demo working on own accounts, over-prepare the screencast/onboarding flow.
2. **Rate limits** across three different models (BUC points / ops-day / RPM) — mitigate: centralized pacing, cache insights, batch mutations.
3. **Automation acting on noisy data** → wasted spend / client trust loss — mitigate: significance floors, cooldowns, dry-run, kill-switch, audit log.
4. **Overspend from platform delivery quirks** (2x/30.4x) — mitigate: hard caps + auto-pause projection.
5. **Breaking API version changes** (e.g., Google v23.x cadence) — mitigate: version-pinned clients, contract tests.
6. **Token/credential security** — encrypted vault, least-scope OAuth, rotation.
7. **Multi-platform data normalization** (differing attribution windows) — document and label; don't silently merge.

---

## 11. Compliance

- **Meta Platform Terms & Developer Policies** govern all ad-data use. **Advertising data must NOT be combined with third-party/internal PII in a way that identifies an end user**, and must not be used for targeting/profiling outside the stated product functions. Business Verification + App Review enforce this.
- **Automated-rules compliance:** support auto-pausing ads that go "Rejected/Limited"; flag sensitive verticals (health, politics, finance) which have extra restrictions.
- **Data handling / PII:** store OAuth tokens encrypted; minimize PII; per-platform data-retention policy; GDPR/consent for any audience data; per-org data isolation (multi-tenant); full audit log of every mutation.
- **TikTok:** passes a data-security compliance audit; respect content/visibility rules.
- **Google:** Required Minimum Functionality + policy compliance for Standard access.

Sources: [Meta platform terms/PII](https://www.adamigo.ai/blog/meta-conversion-data-compliance-best-practices), [Meta GDPR](https://www.adamigo.ai/blog/meta-ads-and-gdpr-compliance-guide), [Meta ad guidelines](https://adsuploader.com/blog/meta-ad-guidelines).

---

### Headline takeaway
The engineering is tractable and largely a normalization + scheduling problem; **the schedule is owned by external API approvals.** Kick off Meta business verification/app review, Google dev-token, and TikTok app review on Day 1 and build read-only against your own accounts while they clear.
